notes: No supplementary files in the input; main article only (11 pages). I1 judged met: the paper's own gravimetric (TG, Cahn TG2121, buoyancy and quartz-blank corrected, H2 99.9995%) H2 'capacity' values are reported in wt.% (Table 2, p. 9: 0.51-3.41 wt.%; Fig. 9, 10-12; text p. 7: 'maximum weight changes ... 3.41 +/- 0.05 wt.% and 1.36 +/- 0.03 wt.%'). Caveat for the extraction stage: the measurement is non-isothermal (temperature cycle 303-673 K, flowing H2 at about 1 atm), the uptake is the weight differential over the heating/cooling cycle, and the authors state it is an assumption that 'the weight change of heating/cooling cycles was attributed to hydrogen adsorption/desorption' (p. 9, Section 3.5); this is not TPD alone and not electrochemical. I2: sorbents are MWCNTs (>90% purity), KOH-activated MWCNTs and Co-loaded versions; carbon is the majority component by mass in all (Co at most 14.62 wt.%). I3: pressure is 1 atm ('under one atmosphere', abstract; 'under 1 atm', p. 8); temperature range 303-673 K stated, and the T axes of Fig. 10 and Fig. 11 (300-700 K) show the weight change reaching its maximum at the 303 K end of the cooling (adsorption) branch. I4: the surface areas (BET, N2 at 77 K, Section 2.5) are for the as-prepared and activated CNTs (without Co), which also have reported H2 weight changes (Fig. 9, Fig. 10a); no surface area is reported for the Co-loaded samples. Not retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction notice in the text); original research article, not a review; no statement that the H2 values were published before (ref. [20] by the same authors is cited only for KOH activation of CNTs).
